# PR Baseline never cancels a run for a superseded head

## Context

#20328 (cause 3: job count against 20 org-wide slots). At 15:43Z on 2026-11-05, 21 `PR Baseline` runs sat queued in this repository at ten jobs each. Three of them were for heads that had already been superseded; one was #20332's first head, queued for 64 minutes. No other PR workflow leaves superseded runs alive. `pr-baseline.yml` has no `concurrency` block, while sixteen sibling PR workflows have one.

## The Problem

A push or a body edit starts a new baseline run, and the previous run keeps its place in the queue. When that run finally starts, it spends ten slots judging a head nobody is proposing any more.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.github/workflows/pr-baseline.yml` calls `neomjs/neo-agent-skills/.github/workflows/reusable-pr-baseline.yml@v0.1.84` on `pull_request: [opened, edited, synchronize, ready_for_review]`. `edited` is there so a corrected body goes green without a push.
- `same-head-check-repair.yml` watches `PR Baseline` and reruns, once, every earlier red run (`cancelled` included) on the same head after a later run passes. A cancelled run on the same head therefore costs a full rerun later.
- #15593 (`build.yml` and the test workflows) set the rerun-safe group: first attempts share one group per ref, and a rerun gets its own (`github.run_attempt == '1' && github.ref || github.run_id`). Otherwise an obsolete rerun cancels the current head's run.

Design authority: #15593: "Normal first-attempt supersession is valuable and must remain: a new commit should cancel expensive work for the previous commit", plus its rerun-safe group.

## The Fix

`pr-baseline.yml` gains:
- `group: pr-baseline-${{ github.run_attempt == '1' && github.ref || github.run_id }}`
- `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event.action != 'edited' }}`

A new head cancels the run for the old one. A body edit waits behind the running run instead of cancelling it, so the same-head repair has nothing to rerun.

A new spec, `PrBaselineConcurrency.spec.mjs`, pins three things: both expressions, and that the repair still watches `PR Baseline`, which is why `edited` must not cancel.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A push to a PR cancels that PR's queued or running baseline run for the previous head.
- [ ] A body edit never cancels a run for the same head, and a rerun never cancels the current head's run.
- [ ] The spec pins the group, the cancel condition and the repair's watch list, red-first.
- [ ] Post-merge: queued baseline runs for superseded heads drop to zero, read from `actions/runs?status=queued`.

## Out of Scope

- Ten jobs into one, and an `edited` run that only needs `pr-body`: neomjs/neo-agent-skills#281.
- Brain's and Institution's own `shared-pr-baseline.yml` callers. Each is its repository's own one-file change.

## Avoided Traps

- **Plain `cancel-in-progress: true`:** a body edit would cancel its own head's run, and the same-head repair would rerun all ten jobs.
- **A ref-only group:** a stale rerun cancels the current head's run (#15593).
